message.content:
The common ancestor of a lion (Panthera leo) and a zebra (Equus quagga) is a **placental mammal that lived during the late Cretaceous‑early Paleogene period**.  
Both species belong to the clade **Laurasiatheria**, which split from other placental mammals around 70–80 million years ago. The last common ancestor of the two lineages would have been a small, generalized mammal that lived in the northern supercontinent Laurasia before the divergence of the carnivoran (lion) and perissodactyl (zebra) lineages.
